q: After a December 31 year-end but before the auditor's report date, a major customer files for bankruptcy because of a steady deterioration in its financial condition over the prior two years. The receivable is material. How should the entity reflect this event?
choices: Adjust the allowance for credit losses at December 31
Disclose the event only, without adjustment
Neither adjust nor disclose because it occurred after year-end
Adjust next year's financial statements
exp: Because the customer's financial deterioration existed at the balance sheet date, the bankruptcy provides evidence about conditions at year-end and is a recognized (Type 1) subsequent event requiring adjustment. Disclosure only applies to conditions arising after the balance sheet date.

q: After year-end but before the financial statements are available to be issued, a fire destroys a nonissuer's main warehouse, causing a material uninsured loss. The financial statements should:
choices: Be adjusted to record the loss at year-end
Disclose the loss without adjusting year-end balances
Ignore the loss because it occurred after year-end
Be adjusted only if the loss exceeds 10% of total assets
exp: A fire after year-end is a condition that arose after the balance sheet date, a nonrecognized (Type 2) subsequent event requiring disclosure if material but not adjustment. Recording the loss at year-end would misstate the conditions that existed then.

q: Which procedure is an auditor of a nonissuer required to perform to identify subsequent events under AU-C 560?
choices: Confirm all year-end receivables again at the report date
Reperform year-end cutoff tests at the report date
Read minutes of meetings of owners, management, and those charged with governance held after the period end and inquire about matters discussed at meetings for which minutes are not yet available
Obtain a legal letter dated after the report release date
exp: AU-C 560 requires procedures such as understanding management's procedures, inquiry, reading minutes (and inquiring about meetings without minutes), and reading the latest interim financial statements. Reconfirming receivables is not a required subsequent events procedure.

q: Through what date is the auditor of a nonissuer required to perform procedures designed to identify subsequent events requiring adjustment or disclosure?
choices: The balance sheet date
The date the financial statements are released to users
The end of the look-forward period for going concern
The date of the auditor's report, or as near as practicable
exp: AU-C 560 requires the auditor to perform procedures covering the period from the financial statement date to the date of the auditor's report (or as near as practicable). After the report date, the auditor has no obligation to perform procedures unless facts become known.

q: After the auditor's report date but before the report is released, the auditor becomes aware of a fact that, had it been known at the report date, might have caused the auditor to revise the report. The auditor should first:
choices: Discuss the matter with management and, where appropriate, those charged with governance, and determine whether the financial statements need revision
Release the report as originally dated because no further obligation exists
Withdraw from the engagement
Notify regulators that the report cannot be relied upon
exp: AU-C 560 requires discussion with management and determination of whether the financial statements need revision when the auditor becomes aware of such facts before release. Withdrawal or regulatory notification is not the first step.

q: Six months after issuing an unmodified report, the auditor of a nonissuer discovers that the client's year-end inventory included goods consigned from others, a material error that existed at the report date. The auditor should first:
choices: Recall the report directly from all known users without contacting the client
Discuss the matter with management and, where appropriate, those charged with governance, and determine whether the financial statements need revision
Issue a revised report without involving management
Disregard the matter because the report has been released
exp: Under AU-C 560, when facts that existed at the report date are discovered after release, the auditor discusses the matter with management and TCWG and determines whether the financial statements need revision, and if so inquires how management intends to address it. Ignoring material subsequently discovered facts is inappropriate.

q: Management agrees to revise previously issued financial statements for a subsequently discovered fact. What is the auditor's responsibility?
choices: Issue a letter stating the original report is withdrawn, without further procedures
Perform procedures limited only to reading the revised note
Perform necessary audit procedures on the revision, and issue a new or revised report including an emphasis-of-matter or other-matter paragraph referencing the reason for revision
Require that the entity change auditors
exp: AU-C 560 requires the auditor to perform procedures on the revision and provide a new or revised report, with an emphasis-of-matter or other-matter paragraph describing the reason for the revision and referring to the note. The auditor also considers whether management communicated with users.

q: Management refuses to take steps to inform users that previously issued financial statements should no longer be relied upon after a subsequently discovered material error. After notifying management and those charged with governance, the auditor should:
choices: Take no further action because confidentiality prohibits disclosure
Issue a new adverse opinion and send it only to management
Wait until the next year's audit to address the matter
Take appropriate action to seek to prevent further reliance on the auditor's report, considering legal advice
exp: AU-C 560 requires the auditor, after notifying management and TCWG, to take action to seek to prevent future reliance on the report, which may include notifying regulators and known users, often with legal counsel. Doing nothing leaves users relying on a report the auditor knows is unsupported.

q: A predecessor auditor is asked to reissue its report on prior-year statements that will be presented comparatively with the current year audited by a successor. Before reissuing, the predecessor should:
choices: Read the current-period financial statements, compare the prior-period statements to those previously issued, and obtain representation letters from management and the successor auditor
Reaudit the prior period in full
Redate the report to the successor's report date
Rely solely on the successor's report
exp: AU-C 560 lists these procedures for a predecessor reissuing its report, including written representations from management and the successor. The predecessor generally uses its original report date unless dual dating for a revision.

q: A nonissuer issues common stock in a public offering after year-end but before the financial statements are available to be issued. The financial statements should:
choices: Record the issuance as of year-end
Disclose the issuance as a nonrecognized subsequent event
Ignore the issuance
Present a pro forma balance sheet in place of the historical balance sheet
exp: Issuance of stock after year-end relates to conditions arising after the balance sheet date, so it is disclosed but not recognized. Pro forma data may supplement, but does not replace, historical statements.

q: Lawsuit damages based on an event that occurred before year-end are settled after year-end, before the statements are available to be issued, for an amount materially greater than the accrual. Which treatment is appropriate?
choices: Disclose only, because the settlement occurred after year-end
Recognize the gain or loss in the following year
Adjust the year-end accrual to reflect the settlement amount
Reverse the accrual and disclose the settlement
exp: Settlement of litigation arising from an event before year-end provides additional evidence about conditions at the balance sheet date, so it is a recognized subsequent event and the accrual is adjusted (ASC 855). Disclosure only applies if the underlying event occurred after year-end.

q: When the auditor reissues a report on financial statements that were not revised and no new events require disclosure, the reissued report should be dated:
choices: As of the reissuance date
As of the date the client requests reissuance
As of the end of the current year
As of the original report date
exp: A reissued report uses the original date to avoid implying that subsequent events procedures were performed after that date (AU-C 560). Redating would extend the auditor's responsibility to the new date.

q: After issuing the report, an auditor discovers that a confirmation procedure considered necessary at the time was omitted, and the auditor's other procedures do not compensate. Users are believed to be relying on the report. Under AU-C 585, the auditor should:
choices: Promptly undertake to apply the omitted procedure or alternative procedures that would provide a satisfactory basis for the opinion
Withdraw the report immediately without further procedures
Disregard the omission because the report was already issued
Notify the state board of accountancy
exp: AU-C 585 requires the auditor, if the omission impairs the ability to support the opinion and users are relying on it, to promptly perform the omitted or alternative procedures. Withdrawal is considered only if procedures reveal the statements are misstated or the auditor cannot apply them.

q: Which of the following is a subsequent event that ordinarily requires disclosure but not adjustment?
choices: Collection of a receivable at an amount different from the year-end estimate due to conditions existing at year-end
A business combination completed after year-end
Determination after year-end of the final sales price of goods sold before year-end
Discovery after year-end of an inventory obsolescence condition that existed at year-end
exp: A business combination after year-end does not provide evidence about conditions at the balance sheet date, so it is disclosed, not recognized. The other items provide evidence of conditions at year-end and require adjustment.

q: Management's written representations should be dated:
choices: As of the balance sheet date
As of the date the fieldwork began
As near as practicable to, but not after, the date of the auditor's report
As of the date financial statements are issued
exp: AU-C 580 requires written representations to be dated as near as practicable to, but not after, the date of the auditor's report, so they cover the subsequent events period. Dating them at the balance sheet date would not cover events through the report date.

q: An auditor of a nonissuer dual-dated the report for a subsequent event disclosed in Note 12. For which period is the auditor responsible for subsequent events?
choices: Through the later date for all events
Only through the balance sheet date
Through the release date for all events
Through the original report date for all events, and through the later date only for the event described in Note 12
exp: Dual dating limits the auditor's responsibility for events after the original report date to the specific event disclosed (AU-C 560). Redating, by contrast, extends responsibility for all events to the later date.

q: Which of the following best describes the auditor's responsibility for facts that become known after the report is released?
choices: The auditor has no obligation to perform procedures after release, but if a fact becomes known that would have caused revision of the report, the auditor must respond
The auditor must continue performing subsequent events procedures for one year after release
The auditor must perform quarterly inquiries of management after release
The auditor's responsibility ends permanently at the report date
exp: AU-C 560 provides no obligation to perform procedures after release, but when facts become known that existed at the report date and might have affected the report, the auditor must take the steps prescribed. The responsibility is reactive, not continuous.

q: Which subsequent event would most likely require a nonissuer to adjust its year-end financial statements?
choices: A decline in the market value of investments due to a market crash after year-end
Sale of inventory after year-end at a price below cost that reflects conditions of obsolescence existing at year-end
A loss on a plant destroyed by flood after year-end
Entering into a significant purchase commitment after year-end
exp: Sales after year-end below cost that reflect obsolescence existing at year-end provide evidence of net realizable value at the balance sheet date and require adjustment. Market declines, floods, and new commitments after year-end are nonrecognized events.

q: A nonissuer's financial statements were revised after release due to a subsequently discovered fact. In the new auditor's report, the auditor should:
choices: Use the original report date only, with no explanatory paragraph
Omit any reference to the earlier report
Date the new report no earlier than the date the revised statements are approved and include an explanatory paragraph describing the revision
Include an adverse opinion on the original statements
exp: Under AU-C 560, the new or revised report is dated no earlier than the date of approval of the revised statements (or dual dated) and includes an emphasis-of-matter or other-matter paragraph referring to the note describing the revision. An adverse opinion is not appropriate for statements that have been properly revised.

q: For an issuer audit under PCAOB standards, which standard addresses the auditor's responsibilities when facts existing at the report date are discovered after the report has been issued?
choices: AS 2801, Subsequent Events
AS 3101, The Auditor's Report
AS 2201, An Audit of ICFR
AS 2905, Subsequent Discovery of Facts Existing at the Date of the Auditor's Report
exp: AS 2905 addresses subsequently discovered facts after the report date for issuers. AS 2801 covers subsequent events through the report date.

q: An auditor issued an unmodified report in March. In June, the auditor learns of a customer's bankruptcy filed in May that resulted from a fire in April. Which is the auditor's responsibility?
choices: No action is required because the event did not exist at the report date
Discuss with management whether the statements require revision
Issue a revised report with dual dating
Notify users that the report should not be relied upon
exp: AU-C 560's subsequently discovered facts requirements apply only to facts that existed at the report date; a bankruptcy caused by an April fire arose after the March report. No revision of the issued statements is required.

q: In the current-year audit, the auditor learns of a fact that would have changed the prior-year report, and comparative statements are being issued. Which approach is appropriate under AU-C 560?
choices: Report on the current year only and ignore the prior year
Ensure the prior-period statements are revised as appropriate and include an other-matter or emphasis-of-matter paragraph in the current report on comparatives as needed
Issue an adverse opinion on the current year
Disclaim on the prior year only
exp: When a subsequently discovered fact affects prior statements that are presented comparatively, the prior statements are revised and the auditor's report on the comparatives explains the revision. The current-year opinion is not automatically affected.

q: Which of the following is most likely to be a source of evidence about subsequent events through the report date?
choices: The prior-year working papers
The engagement letter
The entity's latest available interim financial statements and inquiries of management about matters since year-end
The predecessor auditor's report
exp: AU-C 560 requires reading the latest interim statements and inquiring of management about subsequent events. Prior-year papers, the engagement letter, and predecessor reports do not provide information about events after year-end.

q: An auditor of a nonissuer completed fieldwork and dated the report March 1. On April 10, after release, the auditor is asked to provide a report for use in a lender package with no changes to the financial statements. No new events requiring disclosure have come to the auditor's attention. The auditor should:
choices: Redate the report to April 10 and perform no procedures
Perform a new audit
Dual-date the report for the lender package
Reissue the report dated March 1
exp: Reissuing an unchanged report uses the original date (AU-C 560). Redating without procedures would improperly imply responsibility for events through April 10.

q: Which of the following subsequent events requires the auditor's attention most directly because it may require adjustment to the financial statements?
choices: Settlement after year-end of income tax litigation relating to prior years at an amount different from the recorded liability
Declaration of a cash dividend after year-end
Loss of a major customer after year-end due to a competitor's new product
Changes in exchange rates after year-end
exp: Settlement of tax litigation relating to prior years gives evidence about a liability that existed at year-end, requiring adjustment. Dividends declared, customer losses from new events, and post-year-end exchange rate changes are nonrecognized events.

q: After the report release date, an auditor discovers that the client's lawyer had information about an unasserted claim existing at year-end that would have materially changed the financial statements. The auditor determines that persons are relying on the financial statements. Management will not revise. Which is the correct sequence?
choices: Notify the SEC first, then management
Notify management and those charged with governance, then take steps to prevent further reliance on the report
Issue a revised report without management's involvement
Wait one year and reflect it in the next report
exp: AU-C 560 requires the auditor to notify management and TCWG that they should not rely on the report; if they still do not act, the auditor takes appropriate action to prevent further reliance. The auditor cannot unilaterally revise the entity's financial statements.

q: For a nonissuer, the date through which the entity evaluates subsequent events under U.S. GAAP is most typically:
choices: The balance sheet date
The auditor's report date in all cases
The date the financial statements are available to be issued
The date of the annual meeting
exp: Under ASC 855, nonissuers (other than conduit bond obligors) evaluate subsequent events through the date the financial statements are available to be issued and disclose that date. Issuers evaluate through the issuance date.

q: A nonissuer's auditor reissues a report on prior-year financial statements included in a subsequent document, and a subsequent event since the original report date requires disclosure in the statements. How should the reissued report be dated?
choices: As of the reissuance date for the entire report
As of the original report date with no reference to the event
As of the balance sheet date
Dual-dated, using the original date and a later date for the note disclosing the event
exp: AU-C 560 requires a reissued report to be dual dated when the statements are revised to disclose a subsequent event, limiting the later date to the specific note. Redating the entire report extends responsibility for all events.

q: Under PCAOB standards, in which situation must the auditor of an issuer extend subsequent events procedures beyond the original report date?
choices: When an issuer includes the auditor's report in a registration statement filed under the Securities Act of 1933
When the issuer distributes the annual report to shareholders
When the auditor issues a management letter
When the issuer releases quarterly earnings
exp: Under PCAOB AS 4101, inclusion of the auditor's report in a 1933 Act registration statement requires the auditor to perform subsequent events procedures to (or close to) the effective date. Routine distributions and earnings releases do not.

q: During subsequent events procedures, the auditor learns that management signed an agreement after year-end to sell a business segment, and the segment's assets were not impaired at year-end. How should the auditor evaluate the financial statements?
choices: Require the segment to be presented as discontinued operations at year-end
Evaluate whether the agreement is adequately disclosed as a nonrecognized subsequent event
Require the assets to be written down to the sales price at year-end
Ignore the agreement because it relates to the next period
exp: A sale agreement entered into after year-end reflects a decision arising after the balance sheet date, so it is a nonrecognized subsequent event that may require disclosure (ASC 855). Held-for-sale or discontinued classification depends on criteria met at year-end, which were not met here.
